Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Household, washing & chores · Body, health & movement

make the bed verb

also make your bed

classical

Traupman 36, 38, 122
Traupman 38
Traupman 36: mementō sternere lectulum tuum

lectum sternere

sternō, sternere, strāvī, strātum, spread, lay.

Other words

  • lectum concinnāre

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. bed: make a bed; Erasmus

  • lectum īnsternere

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. bed: make a bed; Vives

Examples

  • Surrēxistī? Age, lectum tuum sterne.

    You’re up? Come on, make your bed.composed

See also bed, bedspread, duvet, be awake.

SourcesLewis & Short: sterno

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. bed: make a bed, bedclothes: bedspread, bedclothes: comforter, bed: air mattress, bed: cot, bed: hammock, mosquito net, hot-water bottle, bedclothes: blanket: electric blanket. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 36, 38, 122, 124.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
